GOOD SAMARITAN CLINICAL INTERVENTION MANDATE
✅ SHOULD YOU GIVE FIRST AID: YES (FOLLOW OFFICIAL PROTOCOL)
START IMMEDIATE HANDS-ONLY CPR • PUSH HARD & FAST (100-120 BPM)
CRITICAL WARNINGS: STRICTLY DO NOT DO THIS (COMMON MISTAKES)
  • DO NOT delay CPR to look for a pulse if the person is unresponsive and not breathing.
  • DO NOT stop chest compressions until professional paramedics take over or an AED arrives.
STEP-BY-STEP SAFE CLINICAL ACTIONS (OFFICIAL 2026 PROTOCOL):
  1. Place the person on their back on a firm, flat surface and call 108 immediately.
  2. Place heel of one hand in center of chest, interlock fingers of other hand, keep arms straight.
  3. Push hard and fast (5-6 cm deep at 100-120 compressions per minute to the beat of 'Stayin Alive').
  4. Allow full chest recoil between compressions; switch with another bystander every 2 minutes.

Official 2026 First Aid Handbook

GEMINI AI KNOWLEDGE BASE

12 Clinical Accident & Emergency Protocols (India Emergency 112 / 108)

These certified clinical protocols are directly programmed into Google Gemini 3.1 AI to evaluate emergency truth and guide Good Samaritans.
Call 112
1

The First Minute: What to Do First

முதல் ஒரு நிமிடம்
Safe Action Steps:
  • Make scene safe: check traffic, fire, electricity, chemicals, falling hazards. Use gloves/barrier.
  • Check response: speak loudly, tap shoulders. DO NOT shake someone who may have a spine injury.
  • Call 112/108 on speakerphone. State exact location, number injured, conscious/breathing status.
  • Check breathing: if unresponsive & not breathing normally, start CPR + AED immediately.
Critical Warnings (DO NOT):
  • DO NOT move a seriously injured person unless immediate danger (fire, traffic) or needed for lifesaving care.
  • DO NOT give food, drink or medicines to an injured or unconscious person.
4

Severe Bleeding, Wounds & Nosebleeds

கடுமையான ரத்தப்போக்கு
Safe Action Steps:
  • Apply firm, continuous direct pressure with sterile gauze or clean cloth.
  • If blood soaks through, ADD MORE MATERIAL ON TOP without lifting the first layer.
  • Nosebleed: sit upright and LEAN FORWARD. Pinch soft part of nose for 10-15 minutes continuously.
Critical Warnings (DO NOT):
  • DO NOT remove an embedded object from a wound; apply pressure around it and stabilize it.
  • DO NOT tilt the head back or lie flat during a nosebleed.
5

Burns, Scalds & Chemical Injuries

தீக்காயங்கள் & ரசாயன காயங்கள்
Safe Action Steps:
  • Cool burn immediately under cool running water for AT LEAST 20 MINUTES.
  • Remove jewellery and loose clothing near burn before swelling starts.
  • Cover loosely with clean non-fluffy dressing or clear cling film laid flat over the area.
Critical Warnings (DO NOT):
  • DO NOT use ice, iced water, butter, toothpaste, oils, creams or powders on burns.
  • DO NOT burst blisters or peel stuck clothing.
6

Fractures, Sprains & Road Accidents

சாலை விபத்து & முதுகுத்தண்டு காயம்
Safe Action Steps:
  • Make scene safe, switch off vehicle ignition if safe. Call 112/108.
  • Keep injured parts STILL in position found. Support with padding without forcing straight.
  • Support head and neck in neutral position found to protect spinal cord.
Critical Warnings (DO NOT):
  • DO NOT remove helmet unless essential to open airway or perform CPR and you are trained.
  • DO NOT twist, straighten or sit up someone with suspected spine injury.
  • DO NOT push exposed broken bone back into the wound.
8

Snakebite, Animal Bites & Allergies

பாம்புக்கடி & விலங்குக்கடி
Safe Action Steps:
  • Snakebite: keep person completely still. Immobilise bitten limb with loose splint. Remove tight items.
  • Animal bite (dog/cat): wash wound thoroughly with soap and running water for ABOUT 15 MINUTES. Immediate rabies shot.
Critical Warnings (DO NOT):
  • DO NOT cut, suck, ice, burn, or wash a snakebite wound.
  • DO NOT apply a tight tourniquet to a snakebite.
Source: 2026 First Aid Reference Guide • India Helpline 112 / 108

The Good Samaritan Law & Legal Rights

✓ SECTION 134A (MVA 1988)

இந்திய நல்ல சமாரியர் சட்டம் • Supreme Court Landmark Ruling (WP (C) No. 235/2012)

"Help is a Right, Not a Risk!"

Any person who assists a road accident victim in good faith enjoys 100% legal immunity from police inquiry, hospital bills, and civil/criminal courts.

1 Zero Civil & Criminal Liability

If an accident victim dies or suffers complications during rescue or transport, the Good Samaritan shall NOT be held responsible in civil or criminal law (Section 134A(1)).

2 Right to Complete Anonymity

Rescuers are free to leave immediately. No police officer, doctor, or receptionist can force you to disclose your name, phone number, address, or identity.

3 Zero Hospital Admission Charges

No government or private hospital can demand registration fees or advance deposits from the rescuer. Immediate first-aid stabilization must be rendered free of cost.

4 No Detention by Police or Hospital

A Good Samaritan is not required to wait at the hospital or police station. Once the patient is safely transferred to trauma staff, you can leave unconditionally.

5 Voluntary Witness Examination

Testifying is 100% voluntary. If you choose to be a witness, you can only be examined once, at your chosen location or via video conferencing (Zoom/Cisco).

6 Disciplinary Action for Harassment

Any investigating police officer or hospital staff who attempts to intimidate, harass, or force a Good Samaritan will face immediate departmental disciplinary proceedings.

MOTOR VEHICLES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2019 — SECTION 134A

"134A. Protection of Good Samaritans:

(1) A Good Samaritan shall not be liable for any civil or criminal action for any injury to or death of the victim of an accident observed by him or caused by his negligence in acting, or for any other result of his rendering assistance to him, if such assistance is rendered in good faith.

(2) The Central Government may, by rules, provide for the procedure for questioning and examination of the Good Samaritan, disclosure of personal information of the Good Samaritan and such other related matters.

Explanation: "Good Samaritan" means a person, who in good faith, voluntarily and without expectation of any reward or compensation renders emergency medical or non-medical care or assistance at the scene of an accident.

What Hospitals Must Do (DO'S)

  • Admit accident victim immediately without demanding registration fee.
  • Provide emergency first aid and trauma resuscitation free of charge.
  • Allow the rescuer to depart unconditionally unless they wish to stay.
  • Display Section 134A Good Samaritan Charter prominently in entrance lobby.

What Hospitals & Police CANNOT Do (DON'TS)

  • CANNOT demand Good Samaritan's Aadhaar, phone number, or signature.
  • CANNOT delay medical treatment pending police arrival or FIR.
  • CANNOT compel rescuer to pay for ambulance fuel, medication, or blood.
  • CANNOT summon Good Samaritan to court unless rescuer agrees voluntarily.
